paper.title_en: False vacuum decay in long-range interacting quantum systems
paper.abstract_en: We formulate false-vacuum decay in a mixed-field Ising chain with $r^{-(1+σ)}$ interactions as a spatially nonlocal Euclidean $φ^4$ theory featuring a fractional spatial kinetic term $\sim |q|^σ$. The nonlocal bounce is anisotropic in space-time and develops algebraic spatial tails. Combining thin-wall arguments with numerical solutions of the full nonlocal saddle, we find two nucleation regimes separated by $σ= 1$. For $0<σ<1$, the lifetime exponent scales with the energy bias $h$ of the metastable state as $B\sim h^{-1/σ}$; for $1<σ<2$, the leading Coleman scaling $B\sim h^{-1}$ is recovered, while long-range effects are retained in the subleading correction $\sim h^{σ-2}$. The same exponents are recovered directly within a two-kink description of the Ising chain on the lattice. Our results show that tunable long-range interactions fundamentally reshape bubble nucleation and alter false-vacuum decay in quantum simulators.
